title: Beneficiary Designation Audit
description: Check every account and policy that passes by beneficiary form, so each one matches the rest of your plan.
intro: Beneficiary forms usually override your will, so an outdated form can undo careful planning. Work through each account, request the current designation in writing, and fix any gaps. Repeat this audit after any major life change.

sections.heading: Accounts to check
items: Each employer retirement plan, such as 401(k) or 403(b)
Each traditional and Roth IRA
Each life insurance policy, including employer group coverage
Each annuity
Each bank account with a payable-on-death option
Each brokerage account with a transfer-on-death option
Health savings accounts
529 college savings plans, which use a successor owner instead

sections.heading: Questions for each account
items: Request a written copy of the current designation
Confirm the primary beneficiary is alive and still your choice
Confirm a contingent beneficiary is named
Confirm no ex-spouse or deceased person is listed
Confirm no minor child is named directly
Confirm the shares add up to 100 percent

sections.heading: Fit with your plan
items: Check whether each designation matches your will or trust
Check whether any account should name your trust instead of a person
Check whether any beneficiary receives disability benefits that an inheritance could affect
Check whether per stirpes language is used where you want children of a deceased beneficiary to inherit

sections.heading: After you make changes
items: Keep the confirmation letter or screenshot for each change
Record the date and new beneficiaries on your asset inventory
Set a reminder to repeat the audit in a year
Tell your executor or trustee where the confirmations are kept
